strengths: The paper addresses an important efficiency bottleneck in multimodal models. Combining CLS-attention-based selection with token merging provides a simple, modular way to reduce visual prefixes without redesigning the language model.

PruMerge+ demonstrates a useful accuracy–compression tradeoff across six image benchmarks and two model sizes. With 25% of visual tokens, the 7B model achieves 76.8 versus 78.5 on VQAv2, 57.1 versus 58.2 on TextVQA, and 64.9 versus 64.3 on MMBench.

The Video-LLaVA experiments provide encouraging evidence of transfer without additional training. Table 3 reports broadly comparable performance across three video benchmarks, including an ActivityNet-QA improvement from 45.3 to 48.3 with PruMerge.

The figures clearly communicate the overall pipeline. Tables 4–6 investigate sampling, supplementation, and fine-tuning, and the principal source models, training data, and methodological ingredients are attributed.
weaknesses: The central practical efficiency claim lacks measured validation. Table 2 explicitly reports roofline estimates for LLM prefill, without end-to-end latency, throughput, or measured memory results incorporating token-reduction overhead and variable-length processing. The more accurate PruMerge+ configuration is also not separately profiled.

Important algorithmic inconsistencies hinder reproducibility. Algorithm 1 adds m spatial tokens to m selected tokens, which would increase average retention from 5.5% to approximately 11%, whereas Table 1 reports 25% for PruMerge+. Its loop and output still reference the original m tokens. The neighbor count k and LoRA hyperparameters are unspecified, and the unnormalized neighbor sum is inconsistent with descriptions of weighted averaging.

The strongest baseline comparison is insufficiently controlled. Table 7 does not establish whether ToMe, ATS, EViT, and CrossGet receive the same fine-tuning treatment as PruMerge+; CrossGet results are imported from its paper. Consequently, the reported advantages cannot be confidently attributed to the reduction algorithm under matched training and implementation conditions.

The distinctive adaptive-selection contribution is not isolated experimentally. Table 4 compares against sequential and spatial sampling, but lacks a fixed-budget CLS-attention top-k baseline using identical merging and training. A spatial-only control at PruMerge+'s 25% budget is also missing. These comparisons are needed to establish the benefit of adaptive IQR selection beyond familiar attention-based pruning and additional token coverage.

The claimed O(n) clustering complexity in Section 2.2 is not justified by the described algorithm. Comparing m anchors with n tokens requires O(mnd) similarity computation for feature dimension d, while the full KK^T construction described near Equation 4 is quadratic in n. Linear scaling requires additional assumptions or an implementation that the manuscript does not provide.

Performance-preservation claims overstate the aggressive-compression results. At 7B, PruMerge reduces VQAv2 from 78.5 to 72.0, POPE from 85.9 to 76.3, and MME from 1510.7 to 1350.3. Section 4.1's assertion of improved POPE performance contradicts Table 1. PruMerge+ offers a credible tradeoff, but its evidence should be distinguished from claims about retaining only 5.5% of tokens.
